title: Chapter 8 — Your First 90 Days
intro: The structured ramp from day one to certified floor professional.

sections.title: Week 1-2: Shadow and Absorb
sections.content:
Your first two weeks are about observation, not action. Pair with the best rep on the floor — not the busiest, the best. Watch how they greet. Watch how they discover needs. Watch how they handle objections. Watch how they close.

Observe at least 20 customer interactions before you take your first solo up. Learn the floor layout — where every brand and category lives. Learn the POS system. Learn the delivery process from order to doorstep.

Memorize five products: the best seller in each major category. You do not need to know everything. You need to know five things cold so you have a starting point for any conversation.

sections.title: Week 3-4: Assisted Selling
sections.content:
Start handling greetings and discovery with your mentor nearby. You do the talking. They watch and jump in if needed. Write up sales with supervision — get the paperwork mechanics down so they become automatic.

Start learning one brand family deeply. Not every brand — one. If your store sells a lot of Bosch, learn Bosch. Know the 300, 500, 800 series and Benchmark. Know the story, the selling angles, the competitive positioning. Depth beats breadth at this stage.

sections.title: Month 2: Guided Independence
sections.content:
Take your own ups with your mentor available for T.O.s when you get stuck. Begin your Daily Five calls — yes, even as a new rep. You have past visitors to follow up with from your shadowing period.

Complete IQ Training Zone 1. This is your product knowledge foundation and your selling process framework.

Your first solo close should be celebrated publicly. That moment matters. It is the transition from trainee to producer. Your manager should recognize it in front of the team.

sections.title: Month 3: Independent with Coaching
sections.content:
Full rotation on the floor. You are taking your own ups, handling objections, and closing without a safety net.

Weekly one-on-one with your manager — 15 minutes. Review your close rate, attach rate, and average ticket. These three numbers tell the complete story of your progress.

Set a 90-day goal and measure against it. Something achievable but meaningful — a revenue target, a close rate target, a training completion milestone. Hit it and you have proven you belong.

The buddy system matters through all three months. Your buddy is a peer, not a manager — someone you can ask questions without feeling judged. The buddy is responsible for cultural integration, not just product training.
